title: Benchmark Dataset Record v0.1
description: Turn P6: the minimal contract a common Benchmark Runner accepts as ONE evaluation item, independent of which Agent variant executes it. This schema does NOT fix the real Gold's eventual shape -- domain/agent-comparison/COMPARISON_PLAN.md and the official Gold authoring process own that decision. This Turn's own schema/example use only synthetic fixture ids/values (no real question_id/document_id/expected answer text) -- see domain/agent-comparison/benchmark/README.md. expected_* fields describe what a Grading Scorer checks for, never anything shown to the ModelAdapter -- a Benchmark Runner must never place question/expected_* content directly into a model prompt as ground truth (only the question itself, and only via the SAME AgentInput.question path every variant already uses).

evaluation_item_id.description: This item's own stable identity -- also used as AgentInput.question_id when a Benchmark Runner executes it.

hints.description: Optional, already-resolved AgentInput.hints passthrough (question-analysis.mjs's own hint precedence) -- lets a synthetic fixture pin corp_codes/metric_codes deterministically instead of depending on Korean text extraction.

split.description: Must equal domain/contracts.mjs's EVALUATION_SPLITS -- reused, never redefined, so a benchmark dataset's split vocabulary never drifts from the evaluation-usage-ledger's own.

evaluation_group_id.description: Groups items that must never be split across DEV_TUNE/DEV_CHECK/HOLDOUT (e.g. paraphrases of the same underlying question) -- see chain_component_id for the correction-chain analogue. null means this item belongs to no group.

chain_component_id.description: The decision-respecting-graph maximal-component identity (domain/handoff artifacts) this item's source document belongs to, if any -- items sharing a chain_component_id must also never be split across splits (a later-confirmed correction relation must never let the same underlying disclosure chain leak across DEV_TUNE/DEV_CHECK/HOLDOUT). null means no known chain membership.

expected_answerability.description: Must equal telemetry.mjs's ANSWERABILITY_TO_VALIDATION_STATUS domain -- the Answerability Scorer compares this against the actually-produced validation_status.

allowed_evidence_ids.description: The Citation Scorer's authorized set -- an Agent answer citing an evidence_id outside this set is a citation-authorization failure, independent of whether that evidence_id happened to validate structurally this run.

semantic_slot.description: A human-stable slot name (e.g. "revenue_fy2023") a Fact Coverage Scorer can match on when the real fact_id is not yet known/stable -- at least one of fact_id/semantic_slot should be non-null.

required.description: false marks an optional/bonus Fact that never lowers coverage if missing.

order_index.description: This event's position in the expected chronological sequence, for the Event/Relation Scorer's ordering check.

unit_conversion_allowed.description: false: the Agent answer's own reported unit must equal `unit` exactly, no scale conversion accepted. true: a conversion listed in the active ScoringPolicy's numeric_unit_conversions table is also accepted (never an unlisted, ad-hoc derived calculation).

role.description: Free-text disambiguator (e.g. "contract_amount", "revenue_ratio_pct") for a question with more than one numeric claim.

date_role.description: e.g. DECISION_DATE / CORRECTION_DATE / COMPLETION_DATE / AS_OF_DATE -- a correct date value with the WRONG role is its own distinct Date Claim Scorer error, never silently accepted as a match.
